label: text
text: Emphatic denials have failed to keep secret the fact that drafts for Dr. Sun Yat-sen's army have been collected at treaty ports and shipped to Canton via Hongkong.

label: text
text: By dint of hard work, the Police have cleared the Colony of an influx of undesirables—recruits for the late Dr. Sun's miscreentary armies, "fed up" with Army life, and deserters from-Canton.

label: text
text: As many know, the strongest force in Canton at present is the Yunnanese army under General Yang Hsi-man, himself a native of Yunnan. He is said to be co-operating with Tang Chi-yan, Tuehun of that far-off province which is becoming notorious as having produced several adventuring armies to overrun other provinces.

label: text
text: During the last year or two, Yunnanese have been travelling through Hongkong to join the colours. Most of them, as country yokels with little or no military training, are sent overland to the Yangtsze River, down to Shanghai, where they embark for Hongkong and Canton direct. Others have found their way by road and rail to Haiphong and then to Hongkong.

label: text
text: Recently, recruiting had become a trade. Instead of recruiting sergeants, there were canvassers acting with boarding houses in the ports of shipment. Passages were arranged for the men brought together.

label: text
text: Whether in Canton or in the outlying districts, there could always be found a number either dissatisfied with military life or who had committed a crime. To escape they must get out of Canton. To reach home they must travel through Hongkong. It was only natural that the majority of deserters should take boat down here. For preference they choose a vessel on which there might be Northerners who speak their language.

label: text
text: It is the practice of the steamers in question to tie up at West Point. In course of time, a fair-sized non-Cantonese colony grew up in the Western district. Many were bona fide workmen, seafarers, itinerant traders, hawkers, &c. But in the last few months, there came not a few who, without fixed abode or occupation, were nothing more than human parasites. When any of their fellow provincial came ashore with money, they attempted to sponge on them, and very often a fight resulted. Others took to bullying the law-abiding Northern and Yunnan men in the district, and street rows were very common. A few became adepts at cargo pilfering on the water front, while instances of molestation were reported.

text: Before the nuisance could assume alarming proportions, however, the West Point Police got to work and gradually rounded up every one of the crowd who did not have work or a fixed abode. In almost every case, the men were found to have had some

label: text
text: At the Central Magistracy this morning, before Mr. S. B. B. McElderry, two stokers and four able seamen from the H.M.S. Titania and Brisbane were charged with disorderly conduct, damage to property and assault.

label: text
text: In the first case, four men charged with the offences at the Wan Kan Yuen restaurant, Wanchai, maintained that they acted in self-defence as they were assaulted by the inmates with a bamboo pole. Evidence was given by the restaurant people that the defendants smashed up the articles in the shop and assaulted them on refusing to supply them with drinks at 12.45 this morning. The first defendant was fined $10 on the first charge and the others $5 each. On the other charges they were ordered to pay compensation, $8 each on the second charge and $8 each on the third.

label: text
text: The other case was against the two stokers who entered a house at 11 p.m. yesterday. They pleaded guilty, and were fined $5 each on the first charge. In addition they were asked to pay $1.50 each compensation for the damage to property, and $1 each to an injured girl.

label: text
text: The Magistrate in inflicting the sentences remarked that he was dealing with them leniently in view of their good records as borne out by their officers.

label: text
text: Apart from a request to collaborate with the local offices of the Asiatic Petroleum Company in landing arrangements the Italian Consul-General at Hongkong Comm. S. Carrarry knows nothing of the flight other than what has appeared in Reuter's brief cable. It would seem, however, that the flight has been undertaken in much the same spirit as was D'Oisy's gallant effort, arranged in the first place as a "sporting" affair, but later operated with the full knowledge and sanction of the authorities who have taken in hand the arrangements with the various Governments over whose territories he will pass.

label: text
text: The machine flown by the Italian is a Lorraine seaplane model, built in Italy, and its behaviour in the course of this extremely difficult undertaking will furnish valuable data for the Italian Government.

label: text
text: As this is the first long distance flight to the Far East this year, the progress of Commander Di Pinedo will be followed with interest and it may be that it will be but the forerunner of many similar attempts, although it is doubtful if other airmen will choose a route which appears a little strange on the face of it. Capt. D'Oisy covered 10,000 miles in something like ninety flying hours, however, and maintained the extraordinary average of about 110 miles per hour, and if it can be done once there is no reason why it should not be done again.

label: text
text: Aviation enthusiasts and the general public will join in wishing the latest aspirant to long distance flying fame a successful voyage and a more fitting entry into the Colony than the two Portuguese airmen who had the hard luck to crash whilst on their way to Macao and to arrive in Hongkong by train!
